library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod_fun <- readModelDb("Clegg_2024_sodiumZirconiumCyclosilicate")
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_fun)
meta <- mod_fun()
```

* Citation: `r meta$reference`
* Description: `r meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13084> (open access; Appendix S1
  holds Table S1, Table S2 and the K+-SZC binding fit of Figure S2)

Clegg 2024 built a fit-for-purpose systems-pharmacology model of potassium
(K+) homeostasis to support development of sodium zirconium cyclosilicate
(SZC), a non-absorbed oral K+ binder. Potassium moves between four
well-mixed compartments: the lumped gastrointestinal (GI) tract, blood
(plasma / serum), tissue extracellular fluid and the tissue intracellular
space. It enters with meals, is lost in faeces from the GI tract and through
the kidneys from blood, and binds reversibly to SZC in the GI tract. Free and
bound SZC leave in faeces at the same rate. Renal clearance scales with eGFR
and follows a sinusoidal diurnal rhythm.

The model was fitted subject by subject (least squares with physiological
penalties) to serum K+ (sK+) from the phase III trials ZS-003 and ZS-004, which
gave a virtual population of 820 parameter sets. That population was then
adapted to two applications: emergency treatment of severe hyperkalaemia
(ENERGIZE design) and K+ control between hemodialysis sessions (DIALIZE
design). The packaged model carries the median of each per-subject parameter
(Clegg 2024 Table 1) as a typical-value model.

## Structure

```{r structure}
data.frame(
  state = mod$state,
  holds = c(
    "K+ in the GI tract (mmol)",
    "K+ in blood / serum (mmol)",
    "K+ in tissue extracellular fluid (mmol)",
    "K+ in the tissue intracellular space (mmol)",
    "free SZC in the GI tract (g)",
    "K+-SZC complex in the GI tract (mmol)"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model states (all amounts).")
```

Doses go into `gi_szc` for SZC (amount in grams) and into `gi_k` for dietary
K+ (amount in mmol, which equals mEq for a monovalent ion). Model time 0 must
be a **midnight**, because the diurnal factor
`m(t) = 1 - p * cos(pi * t / 12)` is written in clock time (lowest at
midnight, highest at noon).

# Population

The model was developed on 820 adults with hyperkalaemia whose per-subject fits
were accepted: 652 of 753 from ZS-003 (sK+ 5-6.5 mmol/L at entry) and 168 of
258 from ZS-004 / HARMONIZE (sK+ >= 5.1 mmol/L). Mean age was 65.3 (SD 12.2)
years and mean weight 89.2 (SD 22.0) kg. 61% were male, 84% White, 13% Black
or African American and 3% other races. Mean eGFR was 44.1 (SD 25.3)
mL/min/1.73 m^2. 55% had chronic kidney disease, 43% type 2 diabetes and 10%
congestive heart failure, and 42% took an ACE inhibitor (Clegg 2024
Table S2). In both trials, SZC (1.25-10 g) or placebo was given three times
daily for 48 h (acute phase). Maintenance followed with once-daily dosing
(ZS-003: same dose or placebo for 12 days; ZS-004: 0, 5, 10 or 15 g for
28 days).

The same information is available programmatically via `meta$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them.

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lr_gb` (r_GB) | log(0.062) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.041, 0.11) |
| `lr_bg` (r_BG) | log(0.23) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.09, 3.8) |
| `lr_eb` (r_EB) | log(3.9) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.14, 49.9) |
| `r_be_eb` (r_BE = 2.3 r_EB) | 2.3 | Table 1 r_BE row; Methods ("r_BE = 2.3 x r_EB") |
| `lr_ei` (r_EI) | log(0.091) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.069, 0.12) |
| `lr_ie` (r_IE) | log(0.0011) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.00083, 0.0015) |
| `lr_cl_k` (r_CL,K) | log(0.0065) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.0036, 0.011) |
| `lr_cl_szc` (r_CL,SZC) | log(0.42) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.26, 0.79) |
| `lr_renal` (r_renal) | log(0.18) 1/h | Table 1, median (IQR 0.13, 0.29) |
| `p_diurnal` (p) | 0.20 | Table 1, median (IQR 0.073, 0.49) |
| `lr_on` (r_on) | log(1503.36) 1/(mM h) | Figure S2c small-intestine k_on 69.6 /(M s), x 3.6 for units, x 6 in vivo (Methods; Figure 2) |
| `lr_off` (r_off) | log(7704) 1/h | Figure S2c small-intestine k_off 2.14 /s |
| `mw_szc` | 410 g/mol | Figure S2 legend ("ZS-9 molecular weight of 410 g/mol") |
| `f_vb` | 0.048 L/kg | Table S1 (20% of ECF, 40% of TBW, 60% of weight); Figure 1 |
| `f_ve` | 0.110769 L/kg | Table S1 (8/13 of TIF, 75% of ECF) |
| `f_vi` | 0.36 L/kg | Table S1 (60% of TBW); Figure 1 |
| `vgi` | 3 L | Table S1; Figure 1; Methods |
| `k_intake` | 100 mmol/day | Methods, Information sources |
| `lr_d` (r_D) | log(1.05) 1/h | Figure 5 flow chart |
| `k_dialysate` | 2 mmol/L | Results; Figure 5 flow chart |
| `d/dt(gi_k)`, `d/dt(blood_k)`, `d/dt(tissue_ecf_k)`, `d/dt(tissue_icf_k)` | n/a | Model equations, Potassium homeostasis |
| `d/dt(gi_szc)`, `d/dt(gi_kszc)` | n/a | Model equations, SZC equations |
| `m(t)` | n/a | Model equations; Model equations text (maximum at noon) |
| initial conditions | n/a | Figure S1 steady-state equations |
| dialysis flux, fixed intracellular K+ | n/a | Figure 1 dialysis bath; Figure 5 flow chart; Results |

## Dimensional analysis

The paper writes its equations in concentrations (mM). The packaged model
multiplies each equation by its compartment volume, so every state is an
amount and every term below is in mmol/h, except `gi_szc`, which is in g/h.

| Term | Units |
|---|---|
| `r_gb * gi_k`, `r_bg * blood_k`, `r_eb * tissue_ecf_k`, `r_be * blood_k`, ... | 1/h x mmol = mmol/h |
| `r_f * m(t) * blood_k`, with `r_f = r_renal * eGFR / 60` | 1/h x (mL/min/1.73 m^2 / mL/min/1.73 m^2) x mmol = mmol/h |
| `bind = (r_on * k_gi * szc_gi - r_off * kszc_gi) * vgi` | (1/(mM h) x mM x mM - 1/h x mM) x L = mmol/h |
| `szc_gi = gi_szc / mw_szc * 1000 / vgi` | g / (g/mol) x (mmol/mol) / L = mM |
| `bind * mw_szc / 1000` in `d/dt(gi_szc)` | mmol/h x g/mol / (mmol/mol) = g/h |
| `RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE * r_d * (k_b - k_dialysate) * vb` | 1/h x mM x L = mmol/h |

# Shared helpers

```{r helpers}
typ_wt <- 89.19 # Table S2 combined mean weight (kg)
typ_egfr <- 44.11 # Table S2 combined mean eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)

# Meals: 100 mmol K+/day, 25% at 8 AM, 33% at noon, 42% at 6 PM (Methods).
meal_events <- function(ndays) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(day = seq_len(ndays) - 1, slot = 1:3) |>
    mutate(
      time = day * 24 + c(8, 12, 18)[slot],
      amt = c(25, 33, 42)[slot],
      cmt = "gi_k",
      evid = 1L
    ) |>
    select(time, amt, cmt, evid)
}

# One subject's event table: meals, optional SZC doses (time, amt in g),
# observations of serum K+ on the blood_k state, and covariate columns.
make_events <- function(ndays, szc = NULL, id = 1L, wt = typ_wt,
                        egfr = typ_egfr, hd_status = 0L, hd_days = NULL,
                        dt = 0.5) {
  obs <- data.frame(
    time = seq(0, ndays * 24, by = dt),
    amt = 0,
    cmt = "blood_k",
    evid = 0L
  )
  szc_ev <- if (is.null(szc) || nrow(szc) == 0L) {
    NULL
  } else {
    data.frame(time = szc$time, amt = szc$amt, cmt = "gi_szc", evid = 1L)
  }
  ev <- bind_rows(meal_events(ndays), szc_ev, obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
  hd_on <- rep(0L, nrow(ev))
  for (d in hd_days) {
    hd_on[ev$time >= d * 24 + 8 & ev$time < d * 24 + 12] <- 1L
  }
  ev |>
    mutate(
      id = id,
      WT = wt,
      CRCL = egfr,
      RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = hd_on,
      RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = hd_status
    )
}
```

# Steady state and mass balance

With a constant K+ intake and no diurnal rhythm (`p_diurnal = 0`), the
Figure S1 initial conditions are the exact steady state, so the solution
must not move.

```{r steady-state}
mod_flat <- mod_fun |> rxode2::ini(p_diurnal = 0)
ev_ss <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, seq(0, 20 * 24, by = 6)),
  amt = c(100 * 20, rep(0, 81)), rate = c(100 / 24, rep(0, 81)),
  cmt = c("gi_k", rep("blood_k", 81)), evid = c(1L, rep(0L, 81)),
  WT = typ_wt, CRCL = typ_egfr, RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 0L,
  RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = 0L
)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_flat, events = ev_ss) |> as.data.frame()
drift <- max(abs(sim_ss$Cc / sim_ss$Cc[1] - 1))
c(sK_mmol_L = sim_ss$Cc[1], max_relative_drift = drift)
stopifnot(drift < 1e-4)
```

The same initial conditions give the K+ balance at steady state. Intake must
equal renal plus faecal loss, and the physiological constraints imposed during
fitting (Figure 1, top-left inset) should hold for the typical subject: at
least 70% of K+ cleared by the kidneys, intracellular K+ 120-150 mM, and
extracellular K+ close to plasma K+.

```{r mass-balance}
th <- as.list(meta$theta)
p <- with(th, list(
  r_gb = exp(lr_gb), r_bg = exp(lr_bg), r_eb = exp(lr_eb),
  r_ei = exp(lr_ei), r_ie = exp(lr_ie), r_cl_k = exp(lr_cl_k),
  r_f = exp(lr_renal) * typ_egfr / 60, r_be_eb = r_be_eb,
  vb = f_vb * typ_wt, ve = f_ve * typ_wt, vi = f_vi * typ_wt,
  r_in = k_intake / 24
))
bal <- with(p, {
  kb <- (r_in / vb * r_gb / (r_cl_k + r_gb)) /
    (r_bg + r_f - r_gb * r_bg / (r_cl_k + r_gb))
  a_gi <- (r_in + r_bg * vb * kb) / (r_cl_k + r_gb)
  ke <- kb * r_be_eb * vb / ve
  ki <- ke * r_ei / r_ie * ve / vi
  data.frame(
    plasma_K_mM = kb, extracellular_K_mM = ke, intracellular_K_mM = ki,
    intake_mmol_h = r_in, renal_mmol_h = r_f * kb * vb,
    faecal_mmol_h = r_cl_k * a_gi,
    renal_fraction = r_f * kb * vb / r_in
  )
})
knitr::kable(t(signif(bal, 4)), col.names = "Typical subject")
stopifnot(
  abs(bal$renal_mmol_h + bal$faecal_mmol_h - bal$intake_mmol_h) < 1e-9,
  bal$renal_fraction >= 0.70,
  bal$intracellular_K_mM > 120, bal$intracellular_K_mM < 150,
  abs(bal$extracellular_K_mM / bal$plasma_K_mM - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The ratio r_BE / r_EB = 2.3 is the ratio of the tissue-extracellular to
blood volume (0.110769 / 0.048 = 2.31), which is why extracellular and plasma
K+ come out equal at steady state, as the Methods state.

# Diurnal profile (Figure 1 inset)

With three meals a day, the typical subject settles into a daily cycle. sK+
peaks near midnight, when renal clearance is lowest, and dips after breakfast.

```{r figure-1}
sim_day <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = make_events(5, dt = 0.25)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time >= 72, time <= 96) |>
  mutate(clock = time - 72)

ggplot(sim_day, aes(clock, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(8, 12, 18), linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after midnight (h)", y = "Serum K+ (mmol/L)",
    title = "Typical-subject daily sK+ profile with meals (dotted lines)",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 1 (top-right inset) of Clegg 2024."
  )

day_summary <- data.frame(
  at_midnight = sim_day$Cc[sim_day$clock == 0],
  at_8am = sim_day$Cc[sim_day$clock == 8],
  daily_variation_pct = 100 * diff(range(sim_day$Cc)) / mean(sim_day$Cc)
)
knitr::kable(signif(day_summary, 3))
# Fits with diurnal variation below 1.7% or above 15% were screened out of the
# virtual population (Methods), so the typical subject must fall inside it.
stopifnot(
  day_summary$daily_variation_pct > 1.7,
  day_summary$daily_variation_pct < 15,
  day_summary$at_midnight > day_summary$at_8am
)
```

The virtual population's simulated mean sK+ was 5.17 mmol/L at 8 AM and 5.59
mmol/L at midnight (Table S2). The typical subject, built from the median of
each parameter, sits about 0.4 mmol/L higher at both times, but the
8 AM-to-midnight rise of 0.4-0.5 mmol/L is reproduced. The median of each
parameter need not give the population-mean output, because sK+ is a
nonlinear function of the parameters.

# ZS-004 dose response (Figure 3, right)

ZS-004 / HARMONIZE gave SZC 10 g three times daily for 48 h, then 0 (placebo),
5, 10 or 15 g once daily for 28 days. The simulation runs in for 3 days on
meals alone, then gives the acute doses with meals (8 AM, noon, 6 PM) and the
maintenance doses at 8 AM. Time is shown in days from the midnight before the
first dose, as in the paper.

```{r figure-3}
runin <- 3
zs004 <- function(maint_g) {
  acute <- data.frame(
    time = as.vector(outer(c(8, 12, 18), (runin + 0:1) * 24, "+")),
    amt = 10
  )
  maint <- data.frame(time = (runin + 2:29) * 24 + 8, amt = maint_g)
  bind_rows(acute, filter(maint, amt > 0))
}
arms <- c(0, 5, 10, 15)
ev_zs004 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), function(i) {
  make_events(runin + 37, szc = zs004(arms[i]), id = i, dt = 1) |>
    mutate(arm = paste0("Maintenance: ", ifelse(arms[i] == 0, "Placebo", paste(arms[i], "g"))))
}))
sim_zs004 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_zs004, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(day = time / 24 - runin)

ggplot(filter(sim_zs004, day >= -1), aes(day, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "purple4") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "blue") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2, xmax = 30, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08, fill = "orange") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Serum K+ (mmol/L)",
    title = "ZS-004: acute 10 g TID, then once-daily maintenance (typical subject)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 (right) of Clegg 2024; shading marks the acute (blue) and maintenance (orange) periods."
  )
```

Clinical sK+ was mostly measured at 8 AM, before the daily dose. The table
compares the typical-subject 8 AM values with the observed arm means read from
Figure 3 (right) by the maintainers.

```{r figure-3-table}
at8 <- function(d) sim_zs004 |> filter(abs(day - (d + 8 / 24)) < 1e-6)
zs004_tab <- bind_rows(
  at8(0) |> mutate(when = "Day 0, 8 AM (baseline)"),
  at8(2) |> mutate(when = "Day 2, 8 AM (end of acute phase)"),
  at8(15) |> mutate(when = "Day 15, 8 AM (maintenance)"),
  at8(29) |> mutate(when = "Day 29, 8 AM (end of maintenance)")
) |>
  select(arm, when, Cc) |>
  mutate(Cc = round(Cc, 2)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = Cc)
knitr::kable(zs004_tab, caption = "Typical-subject sK+ (mmol/L) by ZS-004 arm.")

observed_fig3 <- data.frame(
  arm = c("Placebo", "5 g", "10 g", "15 g"),
  baseline = c(5.7, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5),
  end_acute = c(4.6, 4.5, 4.4, 4.4),
  maintenance = c(5.3, 4.8, 4.5, 4.4)
)
knitr::kable(observed_fig3, caption = "Observed ZS-004 arm means read from Figure 3 (right) of Clegg 2024 (approximate, mmol/L).")

d0 <- at8(0)$Cc
d2 <- at8(2)$Cc
d15 <- at8(15)$Cc
stopifnot(
  # 48 h of 10 g TID lowers sK+ by about 1 mmol/L (observed ~1.0-1.1).
  all(d0 - d2 > 0.6), all(d0 - d2 < 1.6),
  # Maintenance response rises with dose (deterministic, typical subject).
  all(diff(d15) < 0)
)
```

During the acute phase the typical subject falls by
`r round(mean(d0 - d2), 2)` mmol/L, against about 1.0-1.1 mmol/L in the
observed means. Its 8 AM baseline matches the observed arm means.
Maintenance separates the arms in dose order, as observed, but the typical
subject sits 0.2-0.5 mmol/L above the observed arm means. Its placebo-to-15 g
spread is about 0.7 mmol/L, against about 0.9 mmol/L observed. The paper's
own population simulation (Figure 3) tracks the observed means more closely,
because the population mean is not the response of a median subject. After
the last dose the simulated subjects drift back toward their baseline over
days; the paper notes this as a property of the model's structure.

# Emergency treatment of severe hyperkalaemia (Figure 4)

For the ENERGIZE design, Clegg 2024 lowered r_renal by 15% in every virtual
subject to raise baseline sK+ to the trial's mean (6.41 mmol/L simulated,
6.38 observed). They then kept the subjects with sK+ >= 5.8 mmol/L. Baseline
was assumed at 8 PM, and SZC was given as 10 g at 1, 4 and 10 h, 30 g at 1 h,
or 60 g at 1 h. The same r_renal reduction is applied to the typical subject.

```{r figure-4}
mod_er <- mod_fun |> rxode2::ini(lr_renal = log(0.18 * 0.85))
bl_time <- runin * 24 + 20 # 8 PM on the third day
regimens <- list(
  "Placebo" = NULL,
  "SZC 10 g x 3" = data.frame(time = bl_time + c(1, 4, 10), amt = 10),
  "SZC 30 g x 1" = data.frame(time = bl_time + 1, amt = 30),
  "SZC 60 g x 1" = data.frame(time = bl_time + 1, amt = 60)
)
ev_er <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(i) {
  make_events(runin + 2, szc = regimens[[i]], id = i, dt = 0.25) |>
    mutate(regimen = names(regimens)[i])
}))
sim_er <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_er, events = ev_er, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(tad = time - bl_time - 1) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  mutate(cfb = Cc - Cc[abs(time - bl_time) < 1e-6]) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(filter(sim_er, tad >= -4, tad <= 32), aes(tad, Cc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first SZC dose (h)", y = "Serum K+ (mmol/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Emergency dosing, typical subject with r_renal lowered 15%",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 (bottom) of Clegg 2024."
  )
```

The primary end point of ENERGIZE was the change in sK+ from baseline to 4 h
after the first dose (Figure 2), marked by the vertical dashed line in
Figure 4. The maintainers read the population-mean change from baseline at
that line from Figure 4.

```{r figure-4-table}
cfb4 <- sim_er |>
  filter(abs(tad - 4) < 1e-6) |>
  select(regimen, Cc, cfb) |>
  mutate(figure_4 = c(0.05, -0.3, -0.65, -1.2)[match(regimen, names(regimens))])
placebo_cfb <- cfb4$cfb[cfb4$regimen == "Placebo"]
cfb4 |>
  mutate(placebo_corrected = cfb - placebo_cfb) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "sK+ at 4 h (mmol/L)" = Cc,
    "Change from baseline" = cfb,
    "Figure 4 mean change from baseline (approx.)" = figure_4,
    "Placebo-corrected change" = placebo_corrected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Change in sK+ (mmol/L) 4 h after the first SZC dose.")

# Typical-subject changes were within 0.13 mmol/L of the Figure 4 readings
# (largest gap: placebo, +0.18 vs +0.05). A transcription error in the binding
# constants, the SZC mass-to-moles conversion or the GI volume moves the 60 g
# change by far more than 0.35 mmol/L.
stopifnot(all(abs(cfb4$cfb - cfb4$figure_4) < 0.35))
```

The typical subject reproduces the paper's conclusion. 10 g x 3 changes sK+
only modestly within 4 h, and 30 g falls well short of the 1 mmol/L drop that
a mean baseline of 6.4 mmol/L needs to get below 5.5 mmol/L. Only 60 g
reaches it. The typical baseline (6.67 mmol/L) is higher than the population
mean (see above), so even with 60 g its absolute 4-h value only just reaches
5.5 mmol/L. The comparison is therefore made on the change from baseline.

# Hemodialysis (Figure 5)

For the DIALIZE design, Clegg 2024 kept the virtual subjects with eGFR
< 20 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and added a dialysis bath. During sessions blood K+
transfers to a dialysate fixed at 2 mmol/L with r_D = 1.05 1/h. Sessions ran
Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 8 AM to noon. Intracellular K+ was held at its
steady-state value, and r_renal was lowered by 12% to match the pre-dialysis
sK+ in DIALIZE. In the packaged model, `RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE = 1` switches the
dialysis flux on during a session, and `RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = 1` holds
intracellular K+ at its initial steady state.

eGFR enters the model only through the product r_renal x eGFR / 60. The
eGFR < 20 subjects were fitted to sK+ of 5-6 mmol/L, so their own r_renal values
sit far above the population median. Pairing the median r_renal with
eGFR 15 would describe a subject the model never fitted, with a no-dialysis
steady-state sK+ well above 10 mmol/L. The maintainers therefore built a
representative dialysis subject with eGFR 15 whose renal K+ clearance
r_renal x eGFR / 60 equals that of the typical subject, and then applied the
paper's 12% reduction.

SZC 0 (placebo), 5, 10 or 15 g was given once daily at 8 AM on non-dialysis
days. Doses were titrated up by 5 g per week to the target, then held for a
4-week evaluation period, as the paper assumed.

```{r figure-5}
hd_egfr <- 15
mod_hd <- mod_fun |> rxode2::ini(lr_renal = log(0.18 * typ_egfr / hd_egfr * 0.88))
hd_weeks <- 2 + 8 # 2 weeks of dialysis run-in, 4 weeks titration, 4 weeks stable
hd_days <- as.vector(outer(c(0, 2, 4), 7 * (seq_len(hd_weeks) - 1), "+")) # Mon/Wed/Fri
non_hd <- setdiff(seq_len(hd_weeks * 7) - 1, hd_days)
hd_dose <- function(target_g) {
  week <- non_hd %/% 7 - 1 # SZC week 1 starts on day 14
  dose <- pmin(target_g, 5 * week)
  data.frame(time = non_hd * 24 + 8, amt = dose) |> filter(week >= 1, amt > 0)
}
targets <- c(0, 5, 10, 15)
ev_hd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(targets), function(i) {
  make_events(hd_weeks * 7, szc = hd_dose(targets[i]), id = i,
    egfr = hd_egfr, hd_status = 1L, hd_days = hd_days, dt = 0.5) |>
    mutate(group = ifelse(targets[i] == 0, "Placebo", paste0("SZC ", targets[i], " g")))
}))
sim_hd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hd, events = ev_hd, keep = "group") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    day = time / 24,
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Placebo", "SZC 5 g", "SZC 10 g", "SZC 15 g"))
  )

last_week <- (hd_weeks - 1) * 7
ggplot(filter(sim_hd, day >= last_week), aes(day - last_week, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days, Monday 0:00 of the last evaluation week)",
    y = "Serum K+ (mmol/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Hemodialysis Mon/Wed/Fri, SZC on non-dialysis days at 8 AM",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 (bottom right) of Clegg 2024 for a representative subject."
  )
```

The paper compares pre- and post-dialysis sK+ after the last long
interdialytic interval (LIDI, Friday to Monday) of the evaluation period with
DIALIZE (Figure 5, middle right).

```{r figure-5-table}
lidi_monday <- last_week
pre_post <- sim_hd |>
  filter(abs(time - (lidi_monday * 24 + 8)) < 1e-6 | abs(time - (lidi_monday * 24 + 12)) < 1e-6) |>
  mutate(when = ifelse(abs(time - lidi_monday * 24 - 8) < 1e-6, "pre", "post")) |>
  select(group, when, Cc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = when, values_from = Cc)
hd_tab <- pre_post |>
  mutate(
    dialize_pre = c(5.7, NA, NA, NA)[match(group, c("Placebo", "SZC 5 g", "SZC 10 g", "SZC 15 g"))],
    dialize_post = c(3.9, NA, NA, NA)[match(group, c("Placebo", "SZC 5 g", "SZC 10 g", "SZC 15 g"))]
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Pre-dialysis sK+" = pre,
    "Post-dialysis sK+" = post,
    "DIALIZE placebo pre (approx.)" = dialize_pre,
    "DIALIZE placebo post (approx.)" = dialize_post
  )
knitr::kable(hd_tab, caption = "sK+ (mmol/L) around the dialysis session after the last LIDI.")

stopifnot(
  # A 4-h session removes about 2 mmol/L (DIALIZE placebo: 5.7 -> 3.9).
  all(pre_post$pre - pre_post$post > 1.4), all(pre_post$pre - pre_post$post < 3),
  # Pre-dialysis sK+ falls with SZC dose.
  all(diff(pre_post$pre[match(c("Placebo", "SZC 5 g", "SZC 10 g", "SZC 15 g"), pre_post$group)]) < 0)
)
```

For DIALIZE, Figure 5 (middle right) shows the observed SZC-treated
pre-dialysis mean near 5.1 mmol/L and the post-dialysis mean near 3.6 mmol/L.
The paper's population simulations gave a pre-dialysis mean of about
5.5 mmol/L with 5 g, 5.3 with 10 g and 5.1 with 15 g. For the representative
subject the fall in pre-dialysis sK+ per dose step is similar. It starts from
a placebo pre-dialysis value somewhat above the DIALIZE mean of 5.7 mmol/L,
because its parameters were not tuned to the DIALIZE placebo arm the way the
paper's population was.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Typical-value model.** Clegg 2024 fitted each subject separately and did not
  estimate a population model. Table 1 reports only the median and IQR of the
  per-subject estimates, and the packaged model uses the medians. The paper
  states that means and a covariance matrix of the individual parameters were
  provided with an R script as File S1 in Appendix S1. The published
  Appendix S1 (Wiley and PubMed Central, checked 2026-10-29) contains only the
  Word document, so no between-subject variability is encoded and the model
  has no residual error (the fit was penalised least squares). The median of
  each parameter does not reproduce the population-mean sK+; the typical
  subject runs about 0.4 mmol/L above the Table S2 means.
- **SZC dose to concentration.** The equations do not state the units of the
  SZC state. The maintainers converted the SZC mass to moles of K+ binding sites
  with the 410 g/mol that Clegg 2024 used for the in vitro binding fit
  (Figure S2), with one K+ per site and the 3-L GI volume. This gives about
  2.4 mmol K+ binding capacity per gram. The Figure 4 emergency-dosing changes
  and the ZS-004 48-h fall are reproduced to within about 0.1-0.2 mmol/L with
  this conversion.
- **Tissue extracellular volume.** Figure 1 labels the tissue extracellular
  compartment "18% of weight", which is the whole tissue interstitial fluid of
  Table S1 (75% of ECF). Table S1 states that the model's V_E is 8/13 of it,
  0.110769 L/kg. The Table S1 value was used because the fixed ratio
  r_BE = 2.3 x r_EB is described as the volume ratio, and
  0.110769 / 0.048 = 2.31 whereas 0.18 / 0.048 = 3.75.
- **Renal clearance.** The equation writes renal clearance as r_f, and Table 1
  and Figure 1 call it r_renal. They were taken as the same parameter,
  multiplied by eGFR / 60 and m(t) as in the equation and Figure 1.
- **Dialysis flux.** Clegg 2024 describes a one-way transfer of K+ from blood to
  a dialysate bath at a fixed K+ concentration of 2 mmol/L. This was encoded
  as r_D x (K_B - 2 mmol/L), the form in which the dialysate concentration
  matters. The representative subject drops by about 2.4 mmol/L over a session,
  against about 1.8 mmol/L in the DIALIZE placebo arm.
- **Fixed intracellular K+ in hemodialysis.** "Fix intracellular K+ to
  steady-state value" (Figure 5) was encoded as a zero derivative for the
  intracellular state whenever `RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS = 1`. The state then stays
  at its initial no-dialysis steady state for the whole simulation.
- **Dosing times.** The paper used each subject's dosing records and does not
  print the times of the three daily acute doses. The maintainers gave them
  with meals (8 AM, noon, 6 PM). Maintenance doses were given at 8 AM, as in
  the hemodialysis application.
- **Initial conditions.** The Figure S1 steady state under constant intake
  initialises every subject. A run-in of at least 48 h with meals then
  establishes the diurnal cycle before dosing, as in the paper (3 days used
  here).
- **Application adjustments.** The 15% (emergency) and 12% (hemodialysis)
  reductions in r_renal, and the representative dialysis subject's r_renal,
  are made in this article with `rxode2::ini()`. They are not built into the
  packaged model.
- **Observed values** in the comparison tables were read from Figures 3, 4 and
  5 by the maintainers and are approximate (about +/- 0.1 mmol/L).
- No correction notice for Clegg 2024 was found in Europe PMC (searches for
  corrections and the list of citing records) as of 2026-10-29.
